sources.title: Royal Gazette: repeal of the July 2024 sixty-day waiver
sources.publisher: Ministry of Interior / Royal Thai Government Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual one-page Gazette PDF visually read in full; Volume 143, Special Part 207 Ngor, page 28, published 31 August 2026. Clause 1 repeals the 15 July 2024 notice; clause 2 provides commencement fifteen days after publication. Current MFA and PRD implementation notices explicitly identify 15 September 2026.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ให้ยกเลิกประกาศกระทรวงมหาดไทย

sources.title: Royal Gazette: thirty-day tourist exemption for sixty nationalities
sources.publisher: Ministry of Interior / Royal Thai Government Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual four-page Gazette PDF visually read in full, pages 31–34, published 31 August 2026. Clause 2 enumerates all sixty nationalities for tourism; clause 3 limits land-border/land-adjacent-port entries with named exceptions; clause 4 supplies fifteen-day commencement. The corrupt PDF text layer was not used as a substitute for visual inspection.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ให้อยู่ในราชอาณาจักรได้ไม่เกินสามสิบวัน

sources.title: Royal Gazette: replacement visa-on-arrival nationality schedule
sources.publisher: Ministry of Interior / Royal Thai Government Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual one-page Gazette PDF visually read in full, page 30, published 31 August 2026. Clause 1 repeals the July 2024 VOA schedule; clause 2 names only Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia; clause 3 supplies fifteen-day commencement. This instrument does not itself state the length of a VOA stay.
sources.supportingExcerpt: สาธารณรัฐอาเซอร์ไบจาน

sources.title: Royal Gazette: fifteen-day tourist exemption for Seychelles and Mauritius
sources.publisher: Ministry of Interior / Royal Thai Government Gazette
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual one-page Gazette PDF visually read in full, page 29, published 31 August 2026. Clause 1 names Seychelles and Mauritius for fifteen-day tourism; clause 2 limits land-border/land-adjacent-port entries to twice per calendar year with authority for ministerial exceptions; clause 3 supplies commencement.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ให้อยู่ในราชอาณาจักรได้ไม่เกินสิบห้าวัน

sources.title: Current ordinary-passport entry schemes effective 15 September 2026
sources.publisher: Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual full central MFA page and its linked English infographic 2_4.png visually read. Page published/updated 1 September 2026 explicitly confirms commencement; embedded official graphic names sixty 30-day unilateral nationalities, two 15-day nationalities, three VOA nationalities and sixteen bilateral ordinary-passport nationalities. Yellow comparison columns concern Thai nationals travelling outward, not incoming visitor stays.

sources.title: Implementation and transitional treatment of revised tourist entry schemes
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual full official government notice of 4 September 2026 read. It expressly confirms Gazette publication on 31 August, commencement on 15 September, repeal of sixty-day exemption, tourism-only replacement schemes and preservation of permission stamped for entries before commencement.
sources.supportingExcerpt: These measures will therefore take effect from 15 September 2026.

sources.title: Current tourist exemptions and bilateral fourteen-, thirty- and ninety-day routes
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual entire embassy guide read; expressly information as of September 2026 and links the current MFA infographic. Independently lists bilateral 14/30/90-day ordinary-passport groups, Myanmar international-airport restriction, passport validity and exclusion of alien travel documents.
sources.supportingExcerpt: For visits of up to 90 days under bilateral agreements: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Republic of Korea, Peru.

sources.title: Current fifteen-day visa on arrival for Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual entire official embassy guide read; expressly information as of September 2026. Lists only Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia and positively states tourist VOA duration, documentary conditions and exceptional rather than automatic extension.
sources.supportingExcerpt: for a period not exceeding 15 days.

sources.title: THAI E-VISA worldwide application service from January 2025
sources.publisher: Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual entire central MFA announcement of 2 January 2025 read. It establishes worldwide application service outside Thailand; current mission guidance supplies positive all-nationality scope, actual electronic issuance and territorial processing conditions rather than inferring those from portal branding.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Foreign nationals can apply for THAI E-VISA from every corner of the world (except Thailand), starting from January 1, 2025

sources.title: Current visa requirement, electronic issuance, jurisdiction and tourist stays
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual entire current embassy page read, updated 2 October 2026. Explicitly names removal of Mexico/Guatemala/Cuba waiver from 15 September, all visa types processed electronically, no original passport submission, issued visa PDF emailed after approval, any-nationality applications within mission jurisdiction, and sixty-day tourist stay. Does not promise approval or eliminate nationality-specific supporting documents.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Once the application has been approved, the applicant will receive a confirmation email and the e-Visa in PDF format

sources.title: Current all-nationality eVisa eligibility and location restrictions
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual entire embassy FAQ read, updated 29 October 2026. Q1 confirms electronic document submission, Q2 all visa types, Q3 explicitly all foreign nationalities physically in Malaysia, and Q4 rejection outside the mission's processing location. Q7 distinguishes TDAC from a visa. This corroborates nationality-wide electronic eligibility, not unrestricted processing by every mission.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All foreign nationals who are currently in Malaysia are eligible to apply for an e-visa.

policies.title: Sixty ordinary nationalities: thirty-day tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: The adopted September 2026 scheme replaces the former sixty-day unilateral waiver with a thirty-day tourism exemption for these sixty nationalities.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports for short tourist visits, not work, residence, diplomatic/official passports, alien travel documents or individual admission exceptions.
Permission to enter remains subject to a valid recognized passport, entry conditions and immigration inspection; an arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa substitute.
Tourism only. The former sixty-day tourism/short-business exemption was repealed; do not extend this new tourism scheme to short business automatically.

Under Gazette clause 3, entry through land borders or ports adjacent to land borders is limited to twice per calendar year, except nationals of Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia and Singapore and any further ministerially designated exceptions.
For entry before 15 September 2026, existing permission lasts until the immigration-stamped end date; commencement does not force early departure.

policies.title: Seychelles and Mauritius: fifteen-day tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: The adopted September 2026 instrument provides a fifteen-day tourism exemption for Seychelles and Mauritius ordinary passports.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports for short tourist visits, not work, residence, diplomatic/official passports, alien travel documents or individual admission exceptions.
Permission to enter remains subject to a valid recognized passport, entry conditions and immigration inspection; an arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa substitute.
Tourism only. Land-border or land-adjacent-port entries are limited to twice per calendar year, subject to any further ministerially designated exceptions.
Do not confuse this fifteen-day incoming entitlement with outward privileges for Thai nationals shown in the infographic.

policies.title: Cambodia and Myanmar: bilateral fourteen-day visitor exemptions
policies.summary: The current MFA ordinary-passport schedule retains fourteen-day bilateral exemptions for Cambodia and Myanmar; Myanmar's route is restricted to international airports.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports for short tourist visits, not work, residence, diplomatic/official passports, alien travel documents or individual admission exceptions.
Permission to enter remains subject to a valid recognized passport, entry conditions and immigration inspection; an arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa substitute.
Myanmar ordinary-passport exemption applies only through international airports; do not present it as a visa-free land-border permission.
The current record refreshes the bilateral route, not a newly commenced September treaty; no unsupported treaty commencement date is assigned.

policies.title: Nine ordinary passports: bilateral thirty-day visitor exemptions
policies.summary: The current MFA ordinary-passport schedule gives these nine nationalities and territories thirty-day bilateral exemptions.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports for short tourist visits, not work, residence, diplomatic/official passports, alien travel documents or individual admission exceptions.
Permission to enter remains subject to a valid recognized passport, entry conditions and immigration inspection; an arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa substitute.
Hong Kong and Macao entries refer to the catalog's ordinary territorial passports, not every Chinese travel document.
Timor-Leste is thirty days in the current official schedule. This corrects the prior fourteen-day representation without inventing a new treaty commencement date.
This current-read refresh does not claim that these bilateral agreements began on 15 September 2026.

policies.title: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, South Korea and Peru: ninety-day bilateral exemptions
policies.summary: The current MFA ordinary-passport schedule gives these five nationalities ninety-day bilateral exemptions, separate from the new thirty-day unilateral scheme.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports for short tourist visits, not work, residence, diplomatic/official passports, alien travel documents or individual admission exceptions.
Permission to enter remains subject to a valid recognized passport, entry conditions and immigration inspection; an arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa substitute.
Chile is ninety days in the current official schedule. This corrects the prior thirty-day representation without assigning an invented new treaty commencement date.
South Korea and Peru use their longer bilateral ordinary-passport route, not the revoked sixty-day unilateral waiver.
This current-read refresh does not claim that these bilateral agreements began on 15 September 2026.

policies.title: Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia: fifteen-day tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: The replacement Gazette schedule limits ordinary tourist visa on arrival to Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia, with fifteen-day stays confirmed by current consular guidance.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports for short tourist visits, not work, residence, diplomatic/official passports, alien travel documents or individual admission exceptions.
Permission to enter remains subject to a valid recognized passport, entry conditions and immigration inspection; an arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa substitute.
Apply for the visa at an authorized immigration checkpoint; an online VOA application remains a border-issued visa, not a fully issued advance eVisa.
Current consular guidance requires a passport valid at least six months, two blank pages, completed application, photograph, confirmed departure within fifteen days and adequate funds.
Extension is not a standard entitlement; special cases such as illness require immigration consideration.

policies.title: Other ordinary passports: advance electronic tourist visa
policies.summary: The remaining catalog foreign passports require an advance visitor visa and can apply through Thailand's positive all-nationality electronic visa process, subject to mission jurisdiction and approval.
conditions: Applies to ordinary national passports for short tourist visits, not work, residence, diplomatic/official passports, alien travel documents or individual admission exceptions.
Permission to enter remains subject to a valid recognized passport, entry conditions and immigration inspection; an arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa substitute.

The residual cohort is calculated only after the complete current exemption, bilateral and three-nationality VOA schedules. Electronic classification is positively supported by worldwide MFA deployment, all-nationality mission eligibility and emailed issued-visa PDFs, not merely by absence from a waiver list.

Apply outside Thailand to the mission competent for the applicant's current physical location; some missions require residence or country-specific supporting documents. Do not assume any embassy can process every applicant.

The issued tourist visa must be obtained before travel; approval is discretionary. The sixty-day stay is distinct from the visa's entry-validity window; an extension is a separate immigration decision.
The 15 September date is the start of this revised preferred-route cohort after the waiver/VOA replacement, not the launch date of Thailand's eVisa system.
TDAC is a separate arrival declaration, not a visa or ETA. Work, residence, special documents and personal inadmissibility remain separate.

application.label: Official Thai eVisa application
steps: Check the competent Royal Thai Embassy or Consulate for your current physical location and ordinary passport; select the tourist visa matching the intended visit.
Create an account, complete the application and upload the passport, current-location proof and supporting documents requested by that mission; submit payment through the official process.
Wait for approval before travel. The approved electronic visa is sent by email as a PDF; print it and present it with your passport to the airline and Thai immigration.
Complete any required arrival declaration separately and comply with the stay actually permitted by immigration.

unresolved.reason: The new foreign-visitor instruments do not establish a fresh Thai-citizen home-entry finding. Preserve the existing citizenship policy and its actual historical review date; this pass does not relabel citizens as foreign tourists or pretend to reverify their law.
